claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventional ZrB2 processing has densification challenges that lead to porosity and microstructural defects.
Adding a small, well-dispersed silicon-containing sintering aid permits ZrB2 to be sintered at approximately 2000–2100 °C.
The silicon-containing aid enables liquid-phase-assisted sintering of ZrB2.
A transient silicon-rich liquid phase forms at the reduced sintering temperature.
The silicon-rich liquid phase wets ZrB2 grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary wetting by the silicon-rich liquid promotes densification and seals pores.
The silicon additive lowers the effective sintering activation energy through liquid-phase formation.
The liquid phase facilitates particle rearrangement and coalescence.
Particle rearrangement and coalescence reduce the porosity of the sintered ZrB2 ceramic.
Reduced porosity improves the mechanical integrity of the ceramic.
Improved mechanical integrity mitigates hole formation and degradation during prolonged exposure to a corrosive liquid plating bath.
Silicon-aided ZrB2 sintered at 2000–2100 °C will achieve similar or better densification than conventionally prepared ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
Silicon-aided ZrB2 will contain fewer microstructural defects than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Silicon-aided ZrB2 will retain greater structural integrity and resist damage better during long-duration plating-bath exposure.
Conventionally prepared ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C is prone to comparatively high porosity and associated degradation in liquid plating applications.

contradictions.description: The design says the intervention and control groups are sintered under otherwise identical conditions, but assigns them different sintering-temperature ranges. Temperature is the central process variable, so the groups are not processed identically and the design confounds additive addition with sintering temperature.
